suggestions.label: Suggestions
suggestions.ideaPrompt: Use the most suitable technology in this project to create a small “pelican riding a bicycle” piece: an SVG, Canvas animation, or web page. Decide the output format first, then implement it with convincing proportions and motion so it clearly reads as a pelican riding a bike; finish by telling me how to preview it.
suggestions.readmePrompt: Read the project structure and key configuration, then write a clear README covering what it is, the stack, setup/run steps, directory layout, common scripts, and FAQ. Keep it accurate and do not invent commands.
suggestions.bugPrompt: I hit an error. Reproduce it and find the root cause with evidence before fixing it; do not just patch the symptom. Afterward, explain the change, blast radius, and how you verified it.
suggestions.testsPrompt: Inspect the existing test setup and coverage gaps, then add meaningful tests for this feature covering the happy path and key failure paths. Run them and fix what they reveal.
suggestions.apiPrompt: Design a small, stable API: first state the resources, request/response fields, error codes, and authentication. Follow the project's existing style and provide a minimal implementation or interface draft.
suggestions.refactorPrompt: Find one overly long or mixed-responsibility function, split it into smaller modules without changing behavior, explain the boundaries first, then implement and run the relevant tests.
suggestions.scriptPrompt: Write a small script that removes repetitive work. Ask me which workflow to automate, then implement it, explain usage, and actually run it once in this environment to verify.
suggestions.dashboardPrompt: Build a data visualization panel from the project's existing data sources. Confirm the metrics and definitions first, use the smallest dependency set, and handle empty, loading, and error states.
suggestions.riskPrompt: Review the current uncommitted changes: list issues by risk (behavior regressions, edge cases, security, performance) with file/line references and fixes. Do not stop at style comments.
suggestions.stepsPrompt: Break my requirement into executable steps: goal, files touched, acceptance criteria, and dependencies for each. Give me the plan first and wait for my confirmation before changing code.
suggestions.settingPrompt: Add a persisted toggle to the settings page. Reuse the existing settings form and storage path, handle idle/disabled/save-failure states, and verify it survives a restart.
suggestions.releasePrompt: Put together a release checklist covering versioning, build, tests, migrations, rollback, and release notes. Use this project's actual commands instead of generic advice.

standard.label: Standard agent
standard.tagline: Full capability: all tools + every subagent
standard.description: Default main agent: all tools, dispatching every subagent role as needed.

minimal.label: Minimal agent
minimal.description: Keeps only read_file and run_command (command-line file access); subagents limited to General / Explore, and no gates in the architecture graph.

complex.label: Complex agent
complex.tagline: Ten gates: plan → scope → deep dive → implement → review → verify → final review → sweep → goal check
complex.description: All tools + 13 roles (including scope / deep dive / independent re-verification / final review / convergence sweep / goal check); the architecture graph runs G0→G1→G2→G3.5→G4→G5→G6→G7→sweep→goal-check.
